Source slide page 1 (extracted text):
ENGINEERING MATHEMATICS - I
    Unit - 3: Partial Differential Equations



    Department of Science and Humanities

Source slide page 2 (extracted text):
Contents





 1  Problems on Lagrange’s Linear Equation





                                                                                           2 / 10

Source slide page 3 (extracted text):
Solve (mz −ny) ∂z + (nx −lz)∂z = ly −mx                 ∂x              ∂y

The auxiliary equations are   dx  =   dy =   dz                         mz−ny    nx−lz   ly−mx
Using multipliers x, y, z, we get
Each fraction
              x dx + y dy + z dz           x dx + y dy + z dz
   =                       =
      x(mz −ny) + y(nx −lz) + z(ly −mx)          0

           =⇒x dx + y dy + z dz = 0

On integration, it gives
                     x2 + y2 + z2 = c1       (1)

Again using multipliers l, m, n, we get
Each fraction
                          l dx + m dy + n dz                     l dx + m dy + n dz
   =                       =
      l(mz −ny) + m(nx −lz) + n(ly −mx)           0

            =⇒l dx + m dy + n dz = 0

                                                                                           3 / 10

Source slide page 4 (extracted text):
Solve (mz −ny) ∂z + (nx −lz)∂z = ly −mx (contd.)                 ∂x              ∂y





On integration, it gives

                      lx + my + nz = c2       (2)

Hence, from (1) and (2), the required general solution is

                 ϕ(x2 + y2 + z2, lx + my + nz) = 0





                                                                                           4 / 10

Source slide page 5 (extracted text):
Solve x(z2 −y2) ∂z + y(x2 −z2)∂z = z(y2 −x2)                 ∂x               ∂y



Solution. The auxiliary equations are

              dx          dy          dz
              =       =                (1)
             x(z2 −y2)   y(x2 −z2)   z(y2 −x2)

Using multipliers x, y, z, each fraction of (1) is equal to

             x dx + y dy + z dz           x dx + y dy + z dz
                          =
      x2(z2 −y2) + y2(x2 −z2) + z2(y2 −x2)          0


           =⇒x dx + y dy + z dz = 0

On integration
                     x2 + y2 + z2 = C1     (2)





                                                                                           5 / 10

Source slide page 6 (extracted text):
Solve x(z2 −y2) ∂z + y(x2 −z2)∂z = z(y2 −x2) (contd.)                 ∂x               ∂y

Again, (1) can be written as

                 dx          dy          dz
                =       =
                x(z2 −y2)   y(x2 −z2)   z(y2 −x2)

                        dx + dy + dz               dx + dy + dz                        x     y     z               x     y     z
      =                   =
             (z2 −y2) + (x2 −z2) + (y2 −x2)        0

             =⇒dx + dy + dz = 0
                       x    y    z

             =⇒log x + log y + log z = log C2

         =⇒log xyz = log C2 =⇒xyz = C2     (3)

From (2) and (3), the general solution is

                      ϕ(x2 + y2 + z2, xyz) = 0



                                                                                           6 / 10

Source slide page 7 (extracted text):
Solve (y2 + z2)p −xyq + zx = 0



Solution:
Auxiliary equations are

                      dx      dy     dz
                  =   =
                        y2 + z2   −xy   −zx

From the 2nd and 3rd fractions,

                      dy   dz      y
                =      or   = c1
                       y     z       z

Choosing multipliers as x, y, z:

       x dx + y dy + z dz = x(y2 + z2) + y(−xy) + z(−zx) = 0





                                                                                           7 / 10

Source slide page 8 (extracted text):
Solve (y2 + z2)p −xyq + zx = 0 (contd.)





 Integrating,
                         x2 + y2 + z2 = c2

The general solution is

                         y
                  ϕ     , x2 + y2 + z2 = 0
                          z





                                                                                           8 / 10

Source slide page 9 (extracted text):
Solve (x2 −y2 −z2)p + 2xyq = 2xz


Here the auxiliary equations are

                      dx        dy    dz
                    =   =
                     x2 −y2 −z2   2xy   2xz

Taking the last two members, we have

                            dy   dz
                    =
                             y     z

which on integration gives

                           log y = log z + log a

or
                   y             y
                   log  = log a  or   = a        · · · (1)
                     z              z




                                                                                           9 / 10

Source slide page 10 (extracted text):
Solve (x2 −y2 −z2)p + 2xyq = 2xz (contd.)

Using x, y, z as multipliers, we get
Each fraction
                   x dx + y dy + z dz    dz
             =           =
                        x(x2 + y2 + z2)    2xz
or
                   2x dx + 2y dy + 2z dz   dz
                         =
                         x2 + y2 + z2        z
which on integration gives
                    log(x2 + y2 + z2) = log z + log b

or
          x2 + y2 + z2               x2 + y2 + z2
      log          = log b  or         = b        · · · (2)
                z                          z

From (1) and (2), the general solution is
                         x2 + y2 + z2 y
                  ϕ                       ,  = 0
                               z       z

[00:00:04.836] Hello everyone. Welcome back to the course on Engineering Mathematics 1. In this session, we will solve problems on Lagrange's linear equation.
[00:00:20.676] So from theory we understood that the Lagrangius linear equation is given by capital B of XYZ times small p that is dou z by doux plus q of xyz
[00:00:42.532] Q equals R of XYZ.
[00:00:49.604] So in order to solve Lagrangius equation we will use actual equation which is nothing but dx divided by capital B. So dy divided by q and az divided by r
[00:01:08.388] So we can use either grouping or multipliers or both or in some special cases we use exact differential concept also.
[00:01:20.132] On noting these idea, let us solve problems on Lagrangian's linear equation. Let us look at uh yz square divided by x times small p plus x q equals y square.
[00:01:38.532] So this is Lagrangius linear equation, so where this is uh capital P, this is uh capital Q, and this is R. After the selection of PQR, we write the acceler equations.
[00:01:54.532] That is dx divided by y square z over x, dy by x and dz by y square. In order to make simplification easy, let us simplify the first term.
[00:02:09.188] to be x times dx divided by y square z equals dy by x z and dz by y square.
[00:02:20.388] So we have to think uh which method is appropriate after writing such a equation. Should we go for grouping or should we go for multipliers or can go for both.
[00:02:34.116] When we observe these uh actual equations, we can solve this problem by method of grouping because we can separate the variables and uh we can perform integration.
[00:02:45.892] So let's take let us take uh first two fractions uh that is uh x dx uh divided by y square z equals dy and xz. So after cancellation of uh this z and this z and cross and multiplication or after separating the variables.
[00:03:04.996] we'll get x square dx and uh y square dy. So variables have been separated. So we can perform integration. So integration becomes uh x power 3 by 3 equals y power 3 by 3 plus c
[00:03:20.580] And this is same as x power 3 minus y power 3 equals 3c, which is same as some constant a. So the first solution for this problem is going to be x power 3 minus y power 3 equals a. So this looks like u of xyz equals a.
[00:03:39.844] Let us uh search one more solution. Again, when we'll observe this uh exer equation, we can go for grouping again. So if you take a look at this, uh if you take first and the last ratios.
[00:03:54.628] We see that x dx divided by y square z equals dy dz divided by y square. After cancellation of uh y square and this y square, that leads to x into dx equals z time dz. Again variables have been separated.
[00:04:15.204] So on integration uh we get x square by 2, then uh z square by 2 plus some constant c and this is same as x square minus z square equals 2 c and this is same as x square minus uh z square equals b and this is our another solution we have x y z equals b.
[00:04:35.364] As you know from theory, uh once we find out uh these two linearly independent solutions, uh we write the general solution to be phi of u, comma v 0 so which is same as phi of x power 3 minus y power 3 and x square minus z square equals 0.
[00:04:55.460] So in this case uh we took uh the first and second fractions and first and last fractions. If it is possible to take second and third, it is also allowed. So that could be another answer for this problem, if it is possible. So here phi is an arbitrary.

Transcript block 2 (source interval 000300-000599 seconds):
[00:05:16.516] Let us take a look at the second problem. It is uh yzp minus xzq equals xy. So as we know, this is uh capital P, this is capital Q, and uh this is XY. So acceler equations are dx over yz.
[00:05:36.452] Dy divided by minus x and dz by xy. Again we can easily decide we can go for method of grouping in order to find both the solutions.
[00:05:53.700] So from the first and second fractions, uh we get dx by y equals uh dy by minus x. So once we separate variables that leads to x dx plus y dy zero.
[00:06:08.164] After integration that becomes uh x square by 2 plus uh y square by 2 equal to some constant c1. That is same as x square plus y square equal to 2 c1. So that is same as this.
[00:06:27.460] So 2k becomes C1. So this is the first solution for the problem. So to find the second uh solution again we can go for uh uh the first and third fractions uh that gives
[00:06:41.636] Dx by Y Z and Dz by XY After cancellation of this y and this y variables are separated. So that gives DX by Z and Dz by X. So
[00:07:00.036] This is same as
[00:07:05.924] x into dx and z into dz. So x square by two equals z square by two plus some k2. So this is nothing but x square
[00:07:23.140] minus z square equals uh 2k2 so which is same as another constant c2. So finally the general solution for this problem is uh phi of x square plus y square and uh z square minus z square equals 0.
[00:07:42.948] So this is how we can apply method of grouping for a problem to solve Lagrangius linear equation. Let us uh take out another problem Z of Z square plus XY times p x minus q, everything is a product.
[00:08:00.452] So unless we simplify, we will not able to say whether this is a grandious linear equation or not. So once we simplify we see that the equation reduces to uh Xz of Z square plus XY, then uh minus Yz of I mean this is uh capital P
[00:08:20.228] This is going to be capital Q and this is going to be R. So while looking at the actual equation, if you go for first and two fractions after cancellation of uh Z square plus XY and this Z square plus XY we get
[00:08:38.084] uh dx by x equals dy by minus y. And you can cancel this z also. So on integration we get uh log x equals uh minus log y.
[00:08:52.996] So for convenient purpose we can say constant to be log c1. So this is log x plus log y equals log c1. So this gives uh log of xy equals log c1.
[00:09:10.564] So that is MS uh XY equals C1.
[00:09:17.156] So now how do you find out second uh solution that is b equals to b let us take out the first and third fractions so we get the x power 3 dx and uh z power 3 plus xy z tim z.
[00:09:35.268] So this is uh slightly different from uh last uh previous problems. If you take a look at right hand side, unless we solve for this xy, we cannot say this is purely a function of z. In order to do that, we can uh use the previous answer.
[00:09:55.108] that is xy equal to c1 so when you replace x x y by c1 so we get this there so x power 3 dx equals z power 3 plus c1 z time dz now you can see the left hand side we have a x and dx on the right hand side we have z and dz so now you can integrate

Transcript block 3 (source interval 000600-000899 seconds):
[00:10:14.276] So on integration we will get x power 4 by 4. This is uh z power 4 by 4, c1 is constant, z becomes z square by 2 plus another constant, namely c2. So this will be simplified to this x power 4 minus z power 4 plus 2 c1 equals c2.
[00:10:35.044] So again we have to concentrate on C1. So again go back to C1, C1 is XY. So the final answer for this problem is going to be phi of XY and X power 4 minus Z power 4 minus 2 XYZ square equals 0.
[00:10:52.708] So these are the problems on Lagrangius linear equation and uh to find out the solution we use uh the method of grouping. Thank you.
